text:
Mika Zibanejad scored twice in Calgary on Wednesday to stretch his point streak to four games, which is a nice snapshot and a slightly misleading one. The bigger story around the Rangers' center is the shot count. He has 35 shots in 20 games, and his individual expected goals per 60 minutes (the quality of his own chances) sits at 0.68, down from 1.02 last season, when he scored 34. Blue Line Station called it career-low shot volume, and the New York Post has grouped him with J.T. Miller as the heart of the Rangers' scoring problem.

There's another side to it. He has 18 points, 13 of them assists, his finishing is right in line with his chances, and the Post noticed he's been throwing his weight around (28 hits). Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 71% of his exits leaving the zone with possession last season, quieter work that still matters. At 33, the question is whether the shooter comes back. Our season projection still lands at 26 goals (range 20 to 34), so his weekly shot totals are the thing we'd watch.
headline: Zibanejad's points are back, the shots are not
